text:
Dear James,

After reviewing your proposed MSA there are several areas which are not compatible with Ambu’s position. I will need to allocate a resource from Ambu’s legal to deep dive and give a closer look at the key discrepancies. For the time being I can highlight as below, until legal will engage further.

Your proposed MSA is a supplier‑centric SaaS template and is not compatible with Ambu’s Cloud Service contractual model. There are multiple deviations relate to data protection, liability, service continuity, auditability, termination rights, and acceptance, which are core risk‑control mechanisms for Ambu and cannot be accepted as drafted.

Below are some of the areas I have idenfitied

SLA

I could not locate any Service Level Agreements, are these part of a separate appendix? As a minimum we need guaranteed uptime, RPO/RTO, service credits, termination for delay.

Changes to services

We require a fair notice of changes; Ambu needs termination right if change is unacceptable. Impact: Regulatory and operational risk

Data protection & security

As proposed this is an unacceptable exposure for Ambu - Supplier must be fully responsible for security, backup, access control; uncapped liability for data protection breaches.

Audit rights

Current proposal: No audit or assurance rights.
Ambu: Audit rights incl. SOC/ISAE reports and on‑site audits.
Impact: Non‑compliance with Ambu governance requirements

Termination & exit

Ambu requires Termination for convenience (3 months); mandatory exit and migration support.

Liability & indemnities
Ambu requires higher cap (contract value / EUR 500k); unlimited liability for IP, data protection, confidentiality

Data ownership

Ambu owns all Ambu Data; unrestricted access, export, exit assistance, and deletion

subject: RE: Online query from SunTec.ai
text:
Dear Winnie,

Thanks for your email.

As mentioned in our Slack group, I have scheduled our next call for tomorrow morning your time. In the meantime, please allow me to share our detailed findings & cost estimate for your review: -

Project Overview:

The task involves reviewing the video and adding captions for each action performed within the clip. Each caption must clearly describe the hand involved, the action being performed, and the object associated with the action. The captions should accurately represent the sequence of actions observed in the video while maintaining consistency in terminology and description format.

Key Challenges:

*	Videos with repeated actions are easier and faster to process, while videos containing multiple actions and objects require additional review time and careful observation.
*	Actions involving multiple objects require more detailed captions to accurately describe the hand movement, action, and associated objects.
*	Some objects are difficult to identify due to low video quality, motion blur, partial visibility, occlusion, lighting conditions, or similarity between objects, which increases validation time.
*	Rapid hand movements, overlapping actions, or simultaneous actions performed by both hands increase task complexity and require frame-by-frame review.
*	Maintaining consistency in caption structure, object naming, and action terminology across all videos requires additional quality checks and attention during processing.
*	Understanding and becoming familiar with the functionality of the tool.

Skill sets required:

As we have involved 2 junior and 2 senior text annotators on the free POC stage, we have found that it is difficult to expect the right level of productivity and accuracy from junior annotators. We need a mix of mid-level and senior annotators for your project. By doing this, we can expect the necessary quality standards in your project.
